recipes.name: Sunday's Apple Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.1 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed
6 medium tart apples - peeled, cored and sliced

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place a baking sheet on center rack in the oven.
Combine sugar, flour, and cinnamon in a small bowl; set aside. Cut butter into small pieces; divide into 2 equal piles and set each aside.
Roll out 1 crust to an 11- or 12-inch circle; press into a 9-inch pie plate. Roll out remaining 1 crust for top; set aside.
Place sliced apples in a large bowl; pour sugar mixture over top and add ½ butter pieces. Toss apples until thoroughly coated; pour into pie crust in pie plate.
Dot apples with remaining ½ butter. Place top crust over apples. Seal crust edges; cut steam vents in top crust. Set pie plate on the baking sheet in the oven.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is bubbly and crust is golden brown, 50 to 60 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sunday's Apple Pie
raw_recipe.description: Whip up this easy Sunday apple pie recipe featuring store-bought crust, tart apples, sugar, flour, butter, and cinnamon for a last-minute dessert.

review.reviewBody: I really liked this pie recipe! It was simple yet flavorful. The only thing I did differently was to bake the pie at 400 for about 30 minutes to avoid a soggy crust, but will definitely keep this recipe to use for the future. Thanks!

This pie was a big hit! I followed the advice of some other reviewers and added some brown sugar --2 TBL--and about 3/4 tsp of nutmeg. I used the refrigerated Pillsbury pie crusts. Because they were so large, I used only five apples, two Granny Smith and three Pink Lady. Even so, I piled the slices high in the crust and still had a small amount left. I used a tip I found from Sister Pies in Detroit. After chilling the bottom crust, I spread a tablespoon or so of softened cream cheese on the bottom before filling with the apples. I baked the pie for 20 minutes at 425 degrees and then for the remaining 45 minutes at 350. (I used the trimmings from the crust to line a custard cup, and added the remaining apples to make a small "tart".) I took the pie to friends' for dinner, and everyone raved! I'll definitely make it again.

Wow, what an amazing pie. To make the crust, we only used 3 ingredients - 2 cups of flour, 1/2 cup of oil, and 5 tablespoons of water. We used a glass pie dish and as such lowered the temperature to 325 and lengthened the time to about 1 hour. The pie came out with just the right amount of moisture - not dry and not soggy. The taste and texture were perfect. The pie slices were easy to take out of the dish and did not fall apart. We will continue to use this recipe.

Following the advice of others who have rated this recipe, I too added 1/4 cup of brown sugar and 1 tsp nutmeg. However, I find that the filling comes out best if you substitute the flour for corn starch and melt the butter in a skillet then heat the rest of the filling mixture until it starts to thicken. It was a fantastic pie with these changes but without the changes the filling has a tendency to come out too watery.

This worked fine for me because I wanted a recipe that I felt I could skip peeling the apples (arthritis in the hands). I used Gala apples. Instead of all white sugar, I used half brown sugar. I added a faint sprinkle of ground cloves. I baked it for 30 minutes at 375 and an additional 30 minutes at 400 in a 9 inch pyrex pie plate. I covered the edges with foil and took it off the last 5 minutes of baking. When the pie was done, I spread some glaze I had left over from cinnamon buns while the pie was still hot. I used the store brand of refrigerated pie crust. My son said the only change to the recipe should be to put vanilla ice cream on top.

Delicious!!! We use four Gala apples and two Granny Smith and added some walnuts to the apple mixture to give it a bit of crunch, also we brushed melted butter with a dash of sugar 15-20 min. before it finished baking. Everybody loved it!!! A fun recipe to cook with my 8 year old niece!!

Still cooking but it smells great. Used 7 cups of diced green apples and 1 cup sugar - 2 tbsp cinnamon and 2 tbsp apple pie spice with 6 tsps butter (diced small) and 3 tbsp flour mixed it all together and split into 2 pie pans and covered with top crusts. I tried some of the apple mixture before baking and it tastes really good but I love spiced apples.

I basically went by the recipe. However, I used more granny smith apples, less sugar, only 1 tsp. cinnamon, used cornstarch instead of flour and only used about 1 tbsp. butter. After coating sliced apples with sugar mixture I let sit for 10 minutes or so while I made the pastry crust. Scope out apples from bowl and press into pie shell, be sure not to get any of the liquid at the bottom of the bowl. ** I don't like an overpowering taste of cinnamon so I used less. Only used a few butter slices on top of apples before placing top crust. Brushed top of crust with a light coat of melted butter then sprinkled sugar, cinnamon & pumpkin pie spice mixture on it. Baked at 400 for 10 minutes then reduced to 325 for another 45 - 50 minutes. The last 10 minutes I placed a foil tent over pie. It turned out beautiful and was so delicious, my kids loved it. I will be keeping this recipe with the changes though.

This is the first apple pie I have ever made, and following this recipe as well as tweaking it a bit made it come out delish! I used premade pie dough from the grocery store (which tastes almost as good as homemade), and makes making a pie easier and less time consuming. I sprayed my pan with Pam first, and then added about 1/4t nutmeg to my ingredients. I used Gala apples (which are my favorite), but had to use about 8-9 instead of 6, because they were small. I also used 1/4 cup white sugar, and 1/4 cup brown sugar. I also brushed the bottom shell with some butter. I then latticed my top dough, brushed with egg, and sprinkled cinnamon/sugar on top. It came out absolutely perfect at the 350*. I will definitely make again! Thanks for the great recipe!

We loved this pie, yet we added 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1 tsp nutmeg. It made most sense to brush the top crust with egg, like we do with our peach pies. We will definetly make this pie again, with our additions.
Followed this recipe only added a tablespoon of brown sugar a few dashes of nutmeg and teaspoon of vanilla extract baked on 400 for 30 min it was perfect !

Made this exactly as the recipe. It was so good!! I was not sure about the 350 temperature and also not putting something around the crust so it wouldn't get too brown. It works perfectly!! Easy recipe too. No need to over think anything when using this recipe. Thank you for sharing it!
Delicious…. Cooked apples in store bought pre formed pie pastry shells (tenderfl**e). Great apple pie recipe and will use again. Thank you for sharing 🙂
Only change I made to this was add a smidgen of brown sugar. It's in the oven now. Can't wait to try this. Apple pie on the 4th of July!
This recipe is absolutely perfect! No changes necessary!!!
did not set up at all, filing was okay...jusy not my favorite at all
Thank you Donna. During the holidays I add a cup of halved cranberries. Or you can add sliced pears. Be creative and don’t be afraid to adjust spices and sugar to your liking.
AMAZING my family ate this for Thanksgiving! They Loved it! Thanks for the Recipe!

I made this with some additions. I added 1/4 cup water, melted butter on the top crust with sprinkled white sugar on the top. 2 1/2 tbsp cinnamon, and 1/2 tbsp nutmeg.

I also added lemon juice to the sliced apples before I mixed in the glaze.
The best apple pie I’ve ever made. Easy as I followed directions except i changing
